lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Make labelled examples for calibrating a small model from which options of a piece a person picked or rejected, and the lines they named", and give it films (The pieces: { name, gate, decisions, files, units }).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:make-examples-from-picks and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Give films (each piece: name, gate (its pick settings: picked_verdicts and pick_labels with spec_globs using {option}, and optionally words, exclude, rejected_lines, text_keys, spoken_lead_s), decisions (its pick rows: option_id, verdict, lines, reason_verbatim; the last row of an option governs), files (the piece's file paths) and units ({ <spec path>: [{ text, kind, context }] }, the lines of each spec read so far)), and optionally rulings with real and needs (a text ruled directly is left out: the ruling wins), bad_label and rejected (the pattern a rejecting verdict matches, default ^rejected).
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: record:setting (records:read).

worked_examples.title: Make examples from the options a person picked on its own sample
worked_examples.ask: Make labelled examples for calibrating a small model from which options of a piece a person picked or rejected, and the lines they named

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
